title: Using Angular Update Tools knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Using Angular Update Tools”?
options: Using Angular Update Tools should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Using Angular Update Tools helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Using Angular Update Tools means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.

questions.answer_key: Using Angular Update Tools helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Using Angular Update Tools is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “ng update” in this lesson?
options: Connect “ng update” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “ng update” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.

questions.answer_key: Connect “ng update” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “ng update” under Using Angular Update Tools. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Using Angular Update Tools”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
